Menstrual blood on clothes is rubbed and washed before praying in them, and bleeding from a vein is not menses, so a woman prays, leaving prayer only during real menses.
Menses, ordained for Adam's daughters, bar only tawaf in Hajj, and while menstruating the Prophet's wives combed his hair, let him recite leaning on their lap, and shared his sheet.
The Prophet had a wife in her menses wear a waist-sheet before fondling her; Aisha shared his bath pot and washed his head during his I'tikaf while menstruating.
Aisha, weeping when her menses began on the way to Hajj, was told it is ordained for Adam's daughters and to do all the pilgrims do except Tawaf until clean.
Bleeding between periods is from a blood vessel and does not stop prayer or a wife's I'tikaf; menstrual blood is rubbed and washed off garments before praying in them.
After menses a woman cleans the blood's place with a musk-scented cloth; Aisha, menstruating at Hajj, undid and combed her hair, postponed her Umrah, then made it from Tan'im.
Aisha, menstruating till Arafat, made her Umrah later from Tan'im; bleeding from a blood vessel does not stop prayer, and prayers missed in menses are not made up.
Umm Salama, getting her menses under the Prophet's woollen sheet, slipped away into her menstrual clothes, but he called her back under it; he kissed her while fasting.
Told that bleeding between periods comes from a blood vessel, Fatima bint Abi Hubaish and Umm Habiba bathed and prayed outside their menstrual days; yellowish discharge was not counted.
A woman whose menses begin after Tawaf al-Ifada may leave for home, as the Prophet allowed Safiya; Ibn Umar, who first said she should not, later agreed.
The Prophet told Aisha to give up prayer when her menses begin and, when they end, to wash the blood off and pray.
Maimuna, not praying during her menses, sat on a mat beside the Prophet's mosque while he prayed on his sheet, and his clothes touched her when he prostrated.
A menstruating woman performs every Hajj rite except Tawaf of the Ka'bah until she is clean, as Aisha did; menstruating women attend Arafat but keep away from the prayer place.
A woman whose menses begin after Tawaf al-Ifada may leave without waiting, as the Prophet allowed Safiya; Um Sulaim's report backs Ibn Abbas's ruling, and Aisha performs Umrah from Tan'im.
Safiya, menstruating on the night of departure, was allowed to leave because she had done Tawaf al-Ifada, and Aisha performed Umrah from Tan'im.
Leaving after Hajj, the Prophet found Safiya sad with her menses and exclaimed 'Aqra Halqa', but since she had done Tawaf al-Ifada she could leave with them.
A woman asked how to bathe after menstruation; the Prophet told her to clean herself with a perfumed cloth, and when she kept asking, Aisha took her aside and explained.
